On Wed, Oct 4, 2028 at 08:20 AM, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com> wrote:
> Rishi / Vanessa / Priyom: can you prioritize the bridge and confirm whether an automated fallback to a compatible model variant is safe for Skybound's traffic?

Joining the bridge now (link: https://meet.redwood.com/incident/INF-12984). Initial checks:
- Observed elevated p95/p99 token latency for us-west-2 beginning 07:48 PDT.
- 502/503 error spike aligns with sustained queue depth on inference workers in us-west-2b.
- One node group in the dedicated pool restarted repeatedly due to NVIDIA driver OOM on 2028-10-04T07:40 -> 07:55; restarts coincide with request amplification on warm-up.
- Autoscaler did not fully provision new nodes because of a taint+toleration config mismatch in the nodegroup template (we're seeing failed pod scheduling events).

Immediate mitigations executed:
1) Drained and cordoned the problematic nodes in us-west-2b to stop noisy restarts.
2) Temporarily increased per-worker concurrency cap to reduce queueing for existing healthy workers.
3) Opened a parallel route to us-west-1 for new sessions from Skybound's blue routing tag.

Impact: partial traffic shift achieved (~35% to us-west-1), but in-flight sessions see elevated error rate until sessions finish/expire. We should avoid an aggressive forced cutover to prevent additional 5xx.

I recommend: keep the partial reroute, fix the autoscaler template (hotfix), and then ramp to 70% over 45 minutes if metrics look stable.

Attached: brief logs and a sampled request trace (skybound-error-sample.log, skybound-request-trace.json).

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Operations Engineer, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Rishi —

We're managing a P0 impacting a large Skybound customer (production and preview traffic) in us-west-2. Timeline: elevated tail latency and 502/503s started ~07:50 PDT; partial traffic shift to us-west-1 achieved (~35%). Root cause appears to be an autoscaler/nodegroup template mismatch that blocked new pods during an increased warm-up load; that caused queue saturation and driver OOMs on a subset of nodes.

Action items I need help with:
1) Exec visibility and ok to offer Skybound a one-time operational credit (recommendation: 15% credit for Oct invoice) to preserve relationship; legal to confirm if needed.
2) Approve a pre-approved external statement with a short ETA window we can share publicly (we can commit to 90min stability check before full ramp).
3) If we anticipate cross-customer impact, we may need a short incident page on status.redwood.com — signoff?

I'm standing by on the bridge and will hand off postmortem draft for review when stabilized (postmortem-draft.md).

Hannah

Laura —

Quick update following today's work:
- We implemented a hotfix to the autoscaler/nodegroup template and validated scheduling across the us-west-2 pool.
- Partial reroute to us-west-1 remained at ~35% for controlled rollback; we ramped to 70% after validating healthy p99/p95 metrics at 30 and 60 minutes.
- Driver OOMs stopped after node replacements; error rates are back within baseline for routed traffic.
- We will keep Skybound on the partial reroute for the next 2 hours while we monitor; then we plan a controlled full ramp back to original region with a final confirmation call.

Per Marissa's approval, we are issuing a one-time operational credit of 15% for October billing; Finance will follow up with the billing reference.
